paper.title: Certificate-Guided Pruning for Stochastic Lipschitz Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic Lipschitz optimization with noisy evaluations (known L)
unmapped: margin / near-optimality-dimension condition Vol({f >= f* - eps}) <= C eps^(d-alpha) (Assumption 2.3)
settings.definition_quote: Let $(\cX, d)$ be a compact metric space with diameter $D$. We consider $\cX = [0,1]^d$ with Euclidean metric. Let $f: \cX \to [0,1]$ satisfy: ... $|f(x) - f(y)| \leq L \cdot d(x,y)$ ... querying $x$ returns $y = f(x) + \epsilon$ ... The noise $\epsilon$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian ... The goal is to minimize simple regret $r_T = f(x^*) - f(\hat{x}_T)$. We seek PAC guarantees: $r_T \leq \varepsilon$ with probability $\geq 1-\delta$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic Lipschitz optimization with unknown Lipschitz constant (CGP-Adaptive)
unmapped: margin / near-optimality-dimension condition Vol({f >= f* - eps}) <= C eps^(d-alpha) (Assumption 2.3)
learner is given an initial underestimate L0 <= L* of the Lipschitz constant
settings.definition_quote: The theoretical results above assume known $L$, which is often unavailable in practice. ... CGP-Adaptive with initial $\hat{L}_0 \leq L^*$ (learning from underestimation)

symbols.alpha_nod: near-optimality dimension alpha in [0,d] from the margin condition (Assumption 2.3)

conditions: margin condition: Vol({x: f(x) >= f* - eps}) <= C eps^(d-alpha) for all eps > 0
tuning: confidence radius r_i(t) = sigma sqrt(2 log(2 N_t T/delta)/n_i)
oracle access to argmax of score over A_t

source.label: thm:sample_complexity
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:lipschitz}--\ref{ass:margin}, CGP achieves $r_T \leq \varepsilon$ with probability $\geq 1-\delta$ using $T = \tildeO( L^d \varepsilon^{-(2+\alpha)} \log(1/\delta) )$ samples. When $\alpha < d$, this improves upon the worst-case $\tildeO(\varepsilon^{-(2+d)})$ rate.

results.notes: alpha is the near-optimality dimension, not strong convexity; renamed alpha_nod. Proof is a sketchy covering argument; the margin constant C and sigma^2 are hidden in O_tilde.

symbols.alpha_nod: near-optimality dimension alpha in (0,d] from the margin condition

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: For any algorithm and $\alpha \in (0, d]$, there exists $f$ satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:margin} requiring $T = \Omega(\varepsilon^{-(2+\alpha)})$ samples for $\varepsilon$-optimality with probability $\geq 2/3$.

results.notes: Constant success probability 2/3; recorded as high_probability sample complexity. Proof construction is informal (bump among eps^-alpha cells).

symbols.alpha_nod: near-optimality dimension from the margin condition
symbols.K_dbl: number of doubling events, K = ceil(log2(L*/L0)) where L* is the true Lipschitz constant and L0 the initial estimate

conditions: initial estimate L0 <= L* (true Lipschitz constant)
tuning: doubling of L-hat upon detected Lipschitz violation

source.label: thm:adaptive
source.quote: CGP-Adaptive with initial $\hat{L}_0 \leq L^*$ (learning from underestimation) satisfies: ... The number of doubling events is at most $K = \lceil \log_2(L^*/\hat{L}_0) \rceil$. ... After all doublings, $\hat{L} \in [L^*, 2L^*]$ with probability $\geq 1 - \delta$. The total sample complexity is $T = \tildeO(\varepsilon^{-(2+\alpha)} \cdot K)$, i.e., $O(\log(L^*/\hat{L}_0))$ multiplicative overhead.

results.notes: Probability type for item 3 not explicitly stated; inferred high-probability from context. L-dependence (L^d) of Thm 4.8 is dropped here as stated. Proof argument is informal.

symbols.Delta_j: region gap f* - sup_{x in T_j} f(x) of suboptimal trust region j
symbols.c_sigma: constant in the confidence schedule beta_j(n) <= c_sigma sqrt(log(c_T/delta)/n)

conditions: region radii eventually satisfy L*diam(T_j) <= Delta_j/8
within-region replication ensures beta_j(n) <= c_sigma sqrt(log(c_T/delta)/n)
tuning: certified restart rule: restart T_j only if max_{x in T_j} U_t(x) < l_t

source.label: thm:cgp_tr_certified
source.quote: (Allocation bound) Define the region gap $\Delta_j := f^* - \sup_{x\in\cT_j} f(x)$ ... If the region radii are eventually bounded so that $L \cdot \mathrm{diam}(\cT_j) \le \Delta_j/8$, then any suboptimal region $j$ is selected at most $N_j \le \frac{64 c_\sigma^2}{\Delta_j^2}\log\!\left(\frac{c_T}{\delta}\right) + 1$ times before it is eliminated by the certified restart rule.

results.notes: Bound on number of selections of a suboptimal trust region (pull count), recorded as quantity other; holds on good event E (probability >= 1-delta).

symbols.alpha_nod: near-optimality dimension from the margin condition

conditions: estimated local smoothness ratio rho >= 0.5 (CGP continues in Phase 2)

source.label: prop:hybrid
source.quote: CGP-Hybrid achieves: If $\rho \geq 0.5$: same guarantee as CGP, $T = \tildeO(\varepsilon^{-(2+\alpha)})$.

results.notes: Reduces to Theorem 4.8; the rho < 0.5 case gives no explicit rate.
